title: Mathematics
scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Reported precision should match the information available. Leading zeros locate a decimal point but do not count as significant digits; zeros between nonzero digits do count.
For multiplication and division, a common reporting convention uses the fewest significant figures among measured inputs. For addition and subtraction, the limiting decimal place governs.
Exact counts and defined conversion factors do not impose the same significant-figure limit as uncertain measurements. Keep extra digits during intermediate work to reduce rounding error.

A final numerical value and its precision are different aspects of reporting. In this app, dedicated precision questions can require exact text while ordinary numerical questions assess value in a stated unit.

steps.text: For a positive quantity, log10 returns the exponent of ten that produces it. Scientific notation separates a coefficient from its power-of-ten scale.
Multiplication adds exponents and logarithms turn products into sums. A logarithm’s argument should be dimensionless, often formed as a ratio to a reference value.
A change of one unit on a base-ten logarithmic scale represents a tenfold ratio. A negative logarithm is possible for a positive argument below one.
Use order-of-magnitude estimates to check arithmetic. Be explicit whether an axis is linear or logarithmic before interpreting equal spacings.

steps.text: In a right triangle relative to angle θ, sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent.
The hypotenuse lies opposite the right angle, not necessarily opposite the angle named in a problem. Side roles change when the reference acute angle changes.
One full turn is 2π radians or 360°. Small-angle relations such as sin θ ≈ θ require θ in radians and are approximations, not exact identities at every angle.
For components of a vector, identify the angle relative to the chosen axis before assigning sine or cosine. A diagram can make this decision clearer than a memorized word order.

steps.text: Begin a quantitative problem by naming the target and listing given quantities with units. Choose a physical model before rearranging symbols.
Write a symbolic relation, isolate the target and then substitute values. This preserves dependencies and makes unit cancellation easier to inspect.
A plausible number is not sufficient if its unit, sign or limiting behavior is wrong. Check what the formula predicts as a relevant input approaches zero or becomes large.

An approximation must match its regime: small-angle, nonrelativistic, ideal-fluid and constant-acceleration models each have different conditions. State the assumption that makes a shortcut legitimate.
